bibliographic.title: An agentic AI framework for ingestion and standardization of single-cell RNA-seq data analysis
bibliographic.authors: Nima Nouri, Ronen Artzi, Virginia Savova
bibliographic.citation_apa: Nouri, N., Artzi, R., & Savova, V. (2026). An agentic AI framework for ingestion and standardization of single-cell RNA-seq data analysis. npj Artificial Intelligence. https://doi.org/10.1038/s44387-025-00064-0

methodology.method_family: agentic system design and pipeline development
methodology.study_design: two-component framework development (CellAtria agent plus CellExpress pipeline) with architectural description
methodology.sector: biomedical research, pharmaceutical single-cell RNA sequencing
methodology.technology_context: dialogue-driven chatbot interface, graph-based multi-actor agentic AI, LLM-mediated tool orchestration, document-to-analysis automation for scRNA-seq data reuse

inclusion_codes: human oversight mentioned for LLM risk mitigation
eligibility.decision_rationale: The article clearly presents an LLM-based agentic system with a chatbot interface for biomedical data workflows and references institutional, enterprise, and clinical or highly regulated contexts. However, the provided text centers on automating scRNA-seq ingestion and analysis rather than on conversational governance, accountability, auditability, compliance, or oversight mechanisms as an explicit research object. It is relevant as supporting technical evidence, not as central governance evidence.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Full text should be checked for additional governance, oversight, monitoring, traceability, or compliance content beyond the workflow-automation focus visible in the excerpt.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is limited to the excerpt provided. The objective and system architecture are clearly described, but no empirical evaluation sample, user study, or governance-specific validation is visible in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: The description of the CellAtria architecture is internally coherent and technically detailed, but the excerpt offers limited evidence on evaluation rigor, governance mechanisms, or applicability to regulated conversational-AI governance beyond biomedical workflow automation.

coding.theme: Agentic LLM-mediated conversational automation for biomedical data workflows
coding.subtheme: Tool-centric orchestration with limited explicit governance framing
rq_alignment: operational deployment in institutional biomedical settings

synthesis.main_claim: CellAtria is an agentic AI framework that uses an LLM and chatbot interface to orchestrate standardized ingestion and analysis of publicly available single-cell RNA-seq data through pre-validated tools.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a concrete technical architecture for dialogue-driven, LLM-mediated automation in biomedical research workflows, shifting the LLM role from raw code generation to orchestration of robust analytical tools.
synthesis.limitations: The supplied text emphasizes workflow automation and scientific reproducibility more than conversational governance; governance, audit, compliance, and post-deployment monitoring are not developed as primary contributions in the excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on agentic LLM chatbot systems in biomedical or institutional contexts, especially tool-centric orchestration and mentions of oversight in high-risk LLM use; not suitable as central evidence on conversational governance frameworks.
